cards.when: compressing the cross-section of yields by maturity into level/slope/curvature factors (NS/Diebold-Li) or a 4-factor Svensson for a second hump; typically as an input to the recession probit #83
cards.when_not: you want a no-arbitrage/affine term premium (ACM/ABG), or only the simple 10y-2y slope spread, or time-series stationarity/cointegration of one tenor (01/05)

alternatives.criterion: the default macro-factor extraction; few pillars (>=4), stability, interpretability
curves with a second hump, a rich tenor grid (>=6 pillars), a better long-end fit

alternatives.alt: a plain slope spread (10y-2y), outside the category
alternatives.criterion: you only want a recession slope indicator, not a full factor fit
you want a decomposition into expectations versus term premium — outside this card (-> #211)
the natural consumer of the extracted factors — run it after the fit

output_key_fields: model: Nelson.Siegel or Svensson
factors: a date-indexed frame of the factors (Nelson-Siegel: beta_0, beta_1, beta_2, lambda; Svensson: beta_0..beta_3, tau1, tau2)
factors_df: chart-ready data_frame with a date column + factors
fitted_rates: a date-indexed frame of fitted yields per maturity
residuals: a date-indexed frame of observed minus fitted per pillar
which_rate: Spot (default) or Forward (Svensson only)
interpretation: mapping beta_0=level, beta_1=slope, beta_2=curvature,..
n_obs / n_maturities: number of dates / pillars
interpretation_traps: Svensson which_rate: the default MUST be Spot; with Forward the fitted/residuals silently become the wrong quantity (the instantaneous forward instead of the spot) — adversarial-review HIGH
lambda/tau are decay rates (the hump position), NOT yields — do not feed them into a probit as a spread
the sign of the slope depends on the direction of the definition — read the interpretation field, do not assume
this is a descriptive fit, NOT no-arbitrage — it does not separate expectations from the term premium
an inconsistent maturity unit (months/years) distorts lambda and the fit
sources: Diebold-Li 2006, Forecasting the Term Structure of Government Bond Yields, J. Econometrics 130
Nelson-Siegel 1987, J. Business 60
Svensson 1994, IMF WP 94/114
wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE + adversarial-review HIGH (which_rate default=Spot)

cards.method: Parametric yield-curve factor models (Nelson-Siegel / Svensson / cubic spline, Diebold-Li dynamics on a panel) + curve transforms (spot/forward/discount/PCA)
cards.when: you have observed yields by maturity (a single cross-sectional curve AS a vector, or a time series of curves AS a time × maturity matrix) and you want (a) to compress them into level/slope/curvature factors (+ the extra Svensson term) with an explicit decay lambda, or (b) Diebold-Li factor dynamics (a Nelson-Siegel fit per date on a panel), or (c) to produce forward rates / discount factors / spot rates on a free maturity grid, or a PCA (Litterman-Scheinkman) of a yield panel
cards.when_not: you have coupon-bond cash-flow micro data (prices+coupons, not ready spot yields) -> #212 ycnp_estimate (nonparametric); you want a no-arbitrage/affine term-premium decomposition (ACM/ABG expectations vs term premium) — this is a descriptive fit ONLY, out of scope; you only want the simple 10y-2y slope spread (a transform, cat. 00); time-series stationarity/cointegration of one tenor (cat. 01/05); fewer pillars than parameters (NS<4, Svensson<6, cubic<3 = underdetermined)

alternatives.criterion: you want a date-indexed factor series ready to feed the recession probit of #83; or Diebold-Li through the established interface of #87
you want a four-factor Svensson fit on a date-indexed panel, with a spot-or-forward rate choice
you have a coupon-bond cash-flow panel (not ready spot yields); you want a nonparametric time-varying discount/yield surface with no parametric shape
you want empirical (data-driven) level/slope/curvature factors as loadings rather than a parametric Nelson-Siegel fit
you want an expectations against term-premium decomposition — outside this card, which is a descriptive fit only

output_key_fields: yc_fit (one curve): factors {level, slope, curvature}; params (the betas, and tau/tau1/tau2); lambda = 1/tau (Nelson-Siegel: one lambda; Svensson: lambda1 and lambda2; the cubic spline: none); fitted (chart-ready yields); residuals; rmse; plus the curve register handle

yc_fit (a panel, Diebold-Li): factors, a matrix [dates × {level,slope,curvature}]; params [dates × params]; lambda [dates × lambda(s)]; fitted [dates × maturities]; rmse per date; object = the panel matrix (the register handle -> pca)

yc_transform spot: maturity/rate on a grid (yc_predict); forward: maturity/forward_rate (instantaneous, or forward-forward with a horizon); discount: maturity/discount_factor (continuous/annual/semi_annual)
yc_transform pca: loadings [tenors × components]; scores [obs × components]; variance_explained; cumulative_variance; sdev; center; tenors
interpretation_traps: lambda = 1/tau is a decay rate (the hump position/loading), NOT a yield — do not use it as a spread; the NS lambda default comes from tau_init=1, but tau is estimated (optim), so the final lambda differs

the cubic spline has no parametric beta or tau, so lambda is blank; its level, slope and curvature are computed empirically from the curve rather than from beta coefficients — do not compare them one-to-one with the Nelson-Siegel betas
a panel + nelson_siegel = Diebold-Li: an INDEPENDENT fit per row (no common lambda/state space) — for joint dynamics run a VAR on the extracted factors (cat. 03)

the PCA default scale=False (on the covariance) is standard in yield-curve PCA; scale=True (on the correlation) changes the loadings — do not confuse them; the sign of the loadings and scores is arbitrary, since they are identified only up to sign

the maturities must be STRICTLY INCREASING and positive; duplicates or unsorted values are accepted silently by the raw routine (gate); an inconsistent unit — months against years — distorts lambda and the fit
a forward without a horizon = the instantaneous forward; with horizon>0 = a forward-forward rate (between maturity and maturity+horizon) — a different quantity, state it explicitly
n_components in the PCA is capped at min(n_obs-1, n_maturities); exceeding it is silently reduced by the raw routine, and the gate blocks that
sources: Nelson & Siegel 1987 J. Business 60(4); Svensson 1994 IMF WP 94/114; Litterman & Scheinkman 1991 J. Fixed Income 1(1) (the level, slope and curvature factors)
Nelson, C. R., & Siegel, A. F. (1987). Parsimonious Modeling of Yield Curves. Journal of Business, 60(4), 473-489
Svensson, L. E. O. (1994). Estimating and Interpreting Forward Interest Rates: Sweden 1992-1994. IMF Working Paper 94/114
Diebold, F. X., & Li, C. (2006). Forecasting the Term Structure of Government Bond Yields. Journal of Econometrics, 130(2), 337-364
Litterman, R., & Scheinkman, J. (1991). Common Factors Affecting Bond Returns. Journal of Fixed Income, 1(1), 54-61 (PCA level/slope/curvature)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the yields — one curve or a time × maturity panel)
yc_fit (the fit of one curve; register field='object' -> it feeds yc_transform as a handle)
c18_yield_curve/nelson_siegel_svensson.fit_nelson_siegel (the date-indexed baseline; compare the factors before changing method)

cards.method: Arbitrage-free affine (Gaussian) term-structure model — JSZ-style single-country JPS estimation with unspanned macro risks (risk-neutral Q + physical P parameters, model-implied yields, term-premia decomposition)
cards.when: you have a panel of bond yields (zero-coupon yields at many maturities) + macro factors (global & domestic) and you want an arbitrage-free affine model (JSZ/JPS): the risk-neutral (Q) + physical (P) dynamics of the risk factors, the model-implied (fitted) yields, and a DECOMPOSITION of the yield into the expected average short rate (the expectations component) + the TERM PREMIUM; unspanned macro risks (Eco_Act/Inflation) are incorporated beyond the spanned yield factors
cards.when_not: you want a simple static yield-curve fit for one date (Nelson-Siegel or Svensson -> #87/#210); you do not have a multi-maturity yield panel; you want multi-country global-VAR or joint-latent models (they need trade-flow weight matrices and a domestic-unit specification — outside this single-country node); you want a bias-corrected or bootstrap ensemble, or out-of-sample yield forecasts (stochastic and heavy, excluded); macro data outside the strict format (the yield row labels 'Y<mat>M_<economy>', the macro labels '<var> <economy>', and dates as column labels 'dd-mm-yyyy')

alternatives.criterion: you want only a static factor fit of the curve (level/slope/curvature) per date, NOT a dynamic arbitrage-free model with term premia
you want only the Q/P parameters + the maximum log-likelihood (faster, without the fit/term premia)
you want a general Gaussian state-space latent-factor model without no-arbitrage affine bond-pricing restrictions

output_key_fields: max_llk: the maximum log-likelihood of the JSZ MLE estimation
Q_params: the risk-neutral (Q) parameters {K1XQ (the Q-feedback eigenvalues), r0 (the short-rate intercept under Q), se (the measurement-error sd), VarYields (the per-maturity error variance)}
P_params: the physical (P) VAR(1) dynamics of the risk factors {K0Z (the drift), K1Z (the feedback), SSZ (the innovation covariance)}
fitted_yields / observed_yields: (time × maturities) model-implied vs observed yields + fit_rmse (chart-data)
term_premia: (time × maturities) the term-premium component per maturity (chart-data)
expected_component: (time × maturities) the expectations-hypothesis component (the average expected future short rate)
maturities / sample_dates / n_obs / pc_var_explained: sample metadata & the PCA variance of the spanned factors; object = the full ATSMModelOutputs
interpretation_traps: the identity yield = expected_component + term_premia: the term premium is the RESIDUAL above the expected future short rates; a negative term premium is valid (e.g. flight to quality)

the input format is STRICT: yield series 'Y<mat>M_<economy>' (e.g. 'Y120M_Brazil'), macro '<var> <economy>', date column labels 'dd-mm-yyyy'; wrong row labels -> the economy gate blocks it; a wrong data_freq -> a silently wrong annualization of dt

n_factors N = the country-specific SPANNED (yield-derived PCA) factors; N must be < the number of maturities; the macro variables (Eco_Act/Inflation) enter separately as UNSPANNED domestic factors (do not confuse them with N)

single country only: 'JPS original' (domestic-only spanned+macro) vs 'JPS global' (it adds global factors to the P dynamics); GVAR/JLL/JPS-multi were excluded (the trade-weight/domestic-unit machinery)
stationary_Q=True enforces a maximum absolute eigenvalue below 1 under Q, giving a stable long-run curve; False can produce explosive Q dynamics — check K1XQ
DETERMINISTIC (BFGS from a JSZ PCA/OLS initialisation, no RNG) -> no seed; the same input => the same max_llk
sources: Joslin, Singleton & Zhu 2011 Review of Financial Studies 24(3) (a new perspective on Gaussian dynamic term structure models)
Joslin, Singleton & Zhu (2011) 'A New Perspective on Gaussian Dynamic Term Structure Models', Review of Financial Studies 24(3):926-970 (the JSZ canonical form)
Joslin, Priebsch & Singleton (2014) 'Risk Premiums in Dynamic Term Structure Models with Unspanned Macro Risks', Journal of Finance 69(3):1197-1233 (JPS)
Candelon & Moura (2024) 'A Multicountry Model of the Term Structures of Interest Rates with a GVAR', Journal of Financial Econometrics 22(5):1558-1587
Le & Singleton (2018) 'A Small Package of Matlab Routines for the Estimation of Some Term Structure Models', EABCN Training School
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the yield and macro panels as matrices; alternatively leave them unset to use the built-in 'CM_2024' sample)
c18_yield_curve/parametric_yield_curve.yc_fit (a static Nelson-Siegel fit per date — a simpler alternative when you do not need a dynamic arbitrage-free model)
atsm_estimate (the term-premia decomposition is returned inside it: term_premia + expected_component)

cards.method: Nonparametric time-varying yield curve / discount function estimation from coupon-bond cash-flow data (the Koo-La Vecchia-Linton kernel estimator)
cards.when: you have coupon-bond cross-section+time-series micro data (a cash-flow panel: qdate, id, price, tupq=the time to the cash flow in days, pdint=the cash-flow amount) and you want to ESTIMATE non-parametrically the discount function d(tau,t) and the implied yield curve y(tau,t) that EVOLVE over time — without imposing a parametric shape (Nelson-Siegel/Svensson); appropriate for sparse/irregular coupon schedules
cards.when_not: you already have a matrix of spot yields by maturity (zero-coupon rates) — then #87 fit_nelson_siegel/fit_svensson (parametric factor fitting); you want level/slope/curvature factors for macro/probit work — #87; you want an affine term-structure/no-arbitrage model; you do not have cash-flow-level data (only aggregate yields); very few bonds/dates (the kernel estimator needs density around each x)

alternatives.criterion: you already have spot yields by maturity and you want a parametric 3-factor (level/slope/curvature) fit rather than nonparametric cash-flow estimation
a parametric 4-factor (Svensson/Diebold-Li) fit on a ready spot curve

output_key_fields: estimates: records {date, tau, discount, yield} — the estimated discount function + yield curve per (time, maturity) (chart-data)
yield_matrix: a numeric matrix [tau × date] — the yield surface (rows=maturities, cols=dates)
discount_matrix: a numeric matrix [tau × date] — the discount surface
x: the estimation time points (dates); tau: the maturities that were used; span_x; smooth
n_obs (the cash-flow rows), n_bonds (unique ids), n_dates, n_tau; plus the fitted nested estimate table
interpretation_traps: tupq is the time to EACH cash flow in DAYS (not years); pdint is the AMOUNT of the flow (a coupon, or a coupon+face value at maturity) — one row per (bond, cash flow), not per bond

x must lie INSIDE the range of qdate and have enough data around it (the kernel window ~ span_x): an x in a sparse region or at the edges -> non-finite/unstable estimates (the wrapper hard-gates non-finite values)
leaving tau unset lets the routine choose ITS OWN dense maturity grid (the percentiles of the observed maturities) rather than fixed pillars; supply an explicit tau for controlled maturities
span_x is measured in the number of regular intervals between consecutive qdate values (e.g. trading days): a small span_x -> noise/overfitting, a large one -> over-smoothing over time
smooth=True applies a loess over tau; with few tau values it produces 'span too small' warnings — the default False returns the raw estimator points, which are deterministic
yield = -log(discount)/tau (a transformation of the discount factor); it is a continuously compounded spot yield per maturity, NOT a par/coupon yield
sources: Koo, B., La Vecchia, D., & Linton, O. (2021). Estimation of a nonparametric model for bond prices from cross-section and time series information. Journal of Econometrics, 220(2), 562-588
Nelson, C. R., & Siegel, A. F. (1987). Parsimonious Modeling of Yield Curves. Journal of Business, 60(4), 473-489 (the DGP for ycevo_data)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the bond cash-flow panel; the columns qdate/id/price/tupq/pdint)
ycnp_estimate (the estimation returns the estimates + the yield/discount surface matrices inside it)

cards.when: splitting a bond yield into expected future short rates and the term premium, which is what monetary-policy analysis actually needs
cards.when_not: you only need the fitted curve; the sample is too short for the risk-price parameters to be identified

alternatives.criterion: surveys of expected rates are available
fast, robust, the practitioner standard
you want a likelihood-based decomposition

output_key_fields: expected_short_rate: the average expected policy path
term_premium: the residual compensation for risk
fitted_yields: model yields against observed
factors: the pricing factors extracted
interpretation_traps: THE DECOMPOSITION IS NOT UNIQUE: different models attribute very different shares to the premium, and the level of the term premium is far less reliable than its changes
the estimated expected-rate path is heavily influenced by the assumed persistence of the factors, which is poorly identified in short samples
term premium estimates are revised substantially as the sample extends
sources: Adrian, Crump & Moench 2013 (Journal of Financial Economics 110:110-138)
Kim & Wright 2005 (Federal Reserve Board FEDS 2005-33)
pyacm

cards.method: Zero-coupon bootstrapping and spline curve fitting from coupon bonds
cards.when: market instruments are coupon bonds and swaps, and everything downstream needs the zero-coupon curve they imply
cards.when_not: zero rates are already published; the instrument set is too sparse to pin down the curve

alternatives.criterion: exact repricing of the inputs, piecewise curve
a smooth curve that need not reprice exactly
few parameters, smooth by construction

output_key_fields: zero_curve: the fitted zero-coupon curve
discount_factors: on the requested grid
forward_curve: implied forwards
repricing_error: how well the inputs are reproduced
interpretation_traps: BOOTSTRAPPING REPRICES THE INPUTS EXACTLY AND CAN PRODUCE ABSURD FORWARD RATES between nodes; smoothness and exact repricing are in direct conflict
the interpolation rule -- on zeros, on log discount factors, on forwards -- changes the curve materially between nodes
the forward curve is the second derivative of the discount curve and amplifies any roughness enormously
sources: Hagan & West 2006 (Applied Mathematical Finance 13:89-129)
Andersen 2007 (Journal of Computational Finance 10:1)
QuantLib

cards.method: Dynamic Nelson-Siegel in state space with macro factors
cards.when: the yield curve's level, slope and curvature evolve over time, and you want a model that forecasts them and can include macro variables
cards.when_not: you only need a cross-sectional fit at one date; the curve has shapes the three factors cannot represent

alternatives.criterion: cross-sectional fitting only
the factors follow a time-series process
you want yield-macro interaction

output_key_fields: factors: level, slope and curvature paths
loadings: the fixed factor loadings and the decay parameter
forecast: yield-curve forecasts
macro_interaction: cross-effects where macro variables are included
interpretation_traps: THE DECAY PARAMETER IS OFTEN FIXED rather than estimated because the likelihood is nearly flat in it; fixing it at a convention is a decision that affects curvature throughout
the model is not arbitrage free in its basic form, so it must not be used to price derivatives
level, slope and curvature are labels for loadings shapes, not economic objects, and their macro correlations are not causal
sources: Diebold & Li 2006 (Journal of Econometrics 130:337-364)
Diebold, Rudebusch & Aruoba 2006 (Journal of Econometrics 131:309)

cards.method: Shadow short rate at the effective lower bound
cards.when: the policy rate is at its floor, and a curve model without the bound implies negative short rates the market cannot deliver
cards.when_not: the bound never binds in the sample; you want a full macro system rather than a curve construct

alternatives.criterion: no binding bound
the widely used discrete-time construction
a continuous-time alternative with different properties

output_key_fields: shadow_rate: the latent rate, which goes below the bound
expected_lift_off: the expected time to leave the bound
fitted_yields: model yields against observed
bound: the effective lower bound imposed
interpretation_traps: DIFFERENT SHADOW-RATE MODELS PRODUCE VERY DIFFERENT SERIES on the same data -- Wu-Xia and Krippner have disagreed by several percentage points, so the estimate is model, not measurement
the shadow rate is a latent modelling device and is not a policy stance indicator despite being used as one
estimates at the end of the sample are revised heavily as the bound period lengthens
sources: Wu & Xia 2016 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 48:253-291)
Krippner 2013 (Economics Letters 118:135)

cards.method: Bond excess-return predictability and the Cochrane-Piazzesi factor
cards.when: testing whether forward rates predict bond excess returns, which is the empirical case against the expectations hypothesis
cards.when_not: the sample is short relative to the overlapping horizon, where the inference is unreliable regardless of correction

alternatives.criterion: a simple, transparent test
a tent-shaped combination of forwards
you want a structural decomposition instead

output_key_fields: cp_factor: the fitted return-forecasting factor
r_squared: predictive fit per maturity
coefficients: forward-rate loadings, the tent shape
hac_inference: standard errors corrected for overlap
interpretation_traps: OVERLAPPING ANNUAL RETURNS FROM MONTHLY DATA INDUCE STRONG SERIAL CORRELATION; without a HAC or Hodrick correction the t-statistics are inflated by a large factor
the high R2 of these regressions is partly small-sample bias, and out-of-sample performance is far weaker than in-sample fit suggests
the tent shape is not robust across samples and countries, which is the main criticism of the single-factor result
sources: Cochrane & Piazzesi 2005 (American Economic Review 95:138-160)
Fama & Bliss 1987 (American Economic Review 77:680)
Bauer & Hamilton 2018 (Review of Financial Studies 31:399)
statsmodels

arguments.description: A single economy; must exist in yields ('Y<mat>M_<economy>') and dom_macro.

arguments.description: Number of country-specific spanned factors N (>=1, < #maturities).

arguments.description: Names of global variables (row labels of global_macro; default 'Gl_Eco_Act').

arguments.name: dom_var
arguments.description: Names of domestic variables ('<dom_var> <economy>' in dom_macro; default 'Eco_Act').
